summary: Indonesia is a dense economic engine-builder where you race to merge companies into ever-larger conglomerates while managing shipping routes and production capacity to deliver goods to hungry cities. The tension comes from the auction-driven mergers (you set the price, others decide who runs the merged company) and constant zone-of-control jockeying over ports and shipping lanes.
praised: Innovative merger/auction mechanic where the bidder doesn't necessarily end up controlling the result
Deep, satisfying economic engine with real interlocking systems
Strong theme integration for an economic game
High replayability from variable setup and multiple viable strategies
Rewards long-term planning and route optimization
criticised: Long playtime and heavy downtime, especially with 5 players
Steep learning curve and rules overhead for a first play
Can feel very dry or spreadsheet-like to non-economic-game fans
Early mistakes can snowball and leave players uncompetitive for a long stretch
Production of physical components (ships/tiles) sometimes criticized in older printings

interaction.kind: auction-driven mergers and zone-of-control competition over shipping routes and ports

scoring.why: The winner is simply whoever accumulates the most cash by the game's end, driven by efficient production-to-delivery chains
